cd /app && cat > packages/core/src/query/utils/create-query-hash.ts <<'EOF'
import { $internal } from '../../common';
import { isRelationPair } from '../../relation/utils/is-relation';
import type { Relation } from '../../relation/types';
import type { Trait } from '../../trait/types';
import { isModifier } from '../modifier';
import type { QueryHash, QueryParameter } from '../types';

const sortedIDs = new Float64Array(1024); // Use Float64 for larger IDs with relation encoding

export const createQueryHash = (parameters: QueryParameter[]): QueryHash => {
    sortedIDs.fill(0);
    let cursor = 0;

    for (let i = 0; i < parameters.length; i++) {
        const param = parameters[i];

        if (isRelationPair(param)) {
            // Encode relation pair as: (relationTraitId * 1000000) + targetId
            // This ensures unique hashes for different relation/target combinations
            const pairCtx = param[$internal];
            const relation = pairCtx.relation;
            const target = pairCtx.target;

            const relationId = (relation as Relation<Trait>)[$internal].trait.id;
            const targetId = typeof target === 'number' ? target : -1;

            // Combine into a unique hash number
            sortedIDs[cursor++] = relationId * 10000000 + targetId + 5000000;
        } else if (isModifier(param)) {
            const modifierId = param.id;
            const traitIds = param.traitIds;

            for (let i = 0; i < traitIds.length; i++) {
                const traitId = traitIds[i];
                sortedIDs[cursor++] = modifierId * 100000 + traitId;
            }

            // Pair-tracked modifiers must hash differently per target.
            if (param.pairs && param.pairs.length > 0) {
                for (const pair of param.pairs) {
                    const pairCtx = pair[$internal];
                    const relationTrait = pairCtx.relation[$internal].trait;
                    const target = pairCtx.target;
                    const relationId = relationTrait.id;
                    const targetId = typeof target === 'number' ? target : -1;

                    sortedIDs[cursor++] =
                        modifierId * 10000000000 +
                        relationId * 1000000 +
                        targetId +
                        500000000;
                }
            }
        } else {
            const traitId = (param as Trait).id;
            sortedIDs[cursor++] = traitId;
        }
    }

    // Sort only the portion of the array that has been filled.
    const filledArray = sortedIDs.subarray(0, cursor);
    filledArray.sort();

    // Create string key.
    const hash = filledArray.join(',');

    return hash;
};

import { $internal } from '../common';
import type { Entity } from '../entity/types';
import { getEntityId } from '../entity/utils/pack-entity';
import { isRelationPair } from '../relation/utils/is-relation';
import type { Relation } from '../relation/types';

import { getStore } from '../trait/trait';
import type { Trait } from '../trait/types';
import { shallowEqual } from '../utils/shallow-equal';
import type { World } from '../world';
import { isModifier } from './modifier';
import { setChanged } from './modifiers/changed';
import type {
    InstancesFromParameters,
    QueryInstance,
    QueryParameter,
    QueryResult,
    QueryResultOptions,
    StoresFromParameters,
} from './types';

export function createQueryResult<T extends QueryParameter[]>(
    world: World,
    entities: Entity[],
    query: QueryInstance,
    params: QueryParameter[]
): QueryResult<T> {
    const traits: Trait[] = [];
    const stores: Store<any>[] = [];

    getQueryStores(params, traits, stores, world);

    const results = Object.assign(entities, {
        readEach(
            callback: (state: InstancesFromParameters<T>, entity: Entity, index: number) => void
        ) {
            const state = Array.from({ length: traits.length }) as InstancesFromParameters<T>;

            for (let i = 0; i < entities.length; i++) {
                const entity = entities[i];
                const eid = getEntityId(entity);

                // Create snapshots without atomic tracking
                createSnapshots(eid, traits, stores, state);

                callback(state, entity, i);
            }

            return results;
        },

        updateEach(
            callback: (state: InstancesFromParameters<T>, entity: Entity, index: number) => void,
            options: QueryResultOptions = { changeDetection: 'auto' }
        ) {
            const state = Array.from({ length: traits.length });

            // Inline all three permutations of updateEach for performance.
            if (options.changeDetection === 'auto') {
                const changedPairs: [Entity, Trait][] = [];
                const atomicSnapshots: any[] = [];
                const trackedIndices: number[] = [];
                const untrackedIndices: number[] = [];

                getTrackedTraits(traits, world, query, trackedIndices, untrackedIndices);

                for (let i = 0; i < entities.length; i++) {
                    const entity = entities[i];
                    const eid = getEntityId(entity);

                    createSnapshotsWithAtomic(eid, traits, stores, state, atomicSnapshots);
                    callback(state as unknown as InstancesFromParameters<T>, entity, i);

                    // Skip if the entity has been destroyed.

/* @inline */ function getTrackedTraits(
    traits: Trait[],
    world: World,
    query: QueryInstance,
    trackedIndices: number[],
    untrackedIndices: number[]
) {
    for (let i = 0; i < traits.length; i++) {
        const trait = traits[i];
        const hasTracked = world[$internal].trackedTraits.has(trait);
        const hasChanged = query.hasChangedModifiers && query.changedTraits.has(trait);

        if (hasTracked || hasChanged) trackedIndices.push(i);
        else untrackedIndices.push(i);
    }
}

/* @inline */ function createSnapshots(
    entityId: number,
    traits: Trait[],
    stores: Store<any>[],
    state: any[]
) {
    for (let i = 0; i < traits.length; i++) {
        const trait = traits[i];
        const ctx = trait[$internal];
        const value = ctx.get(entityId, stores[i]);
        state[i] = value;
    }
}

/* @inline */ function createSnapshotsWithAtomic(
    entityId: number,
    traits: Trait[],
    stores: Store<any>[],
    state: any[],
    atomicSnapshots: any[]
) {
    for (let j = 0; j < traits.length; j++) {
        const trait = traits[j];
        const ctx = trait[$internal];
        const value = ctx.get(entityId, stores[j]);
        state[j] = value;
        atomicSnapshots[j] = ctx.type === 'aos' ? { ...value } : null;
    }
}

/* @inline */ export function getQueryStores<T extends QueryParameter[]>(
    params: T,
    traits: Trait[],
    stores: Store<any>[],
    world: World
) {
    for (let i = 0; i < params.length; i++) {
        const param = params[i];

        // Handle relation pairs
        if (isRelationPair(param)) {
            const pairCtx = param[$internal];
            const relation = pairCtx.relation as Relation<Trait>;
            const baseTrait = relation[$internal].trait;
            if (baseTrait[$internal].type !== 'tag') {
                traits.push(baseTrait);
                stores.push(getStore(world, baseTrait));
            }
            continue;
        }

        if (isModifier(param)) {
            // Skip not modifier.
            if (param.type === 'not') continue;

            const modifierTraits = param.traits;
            for (const trait of modifierTraits) {
                if (trait[$internal].type === 'tag') continue; // Skip tags
                traits.push(trait);
                stores.push(getStore(world, trait));
            }
        } else {
            const trait = param as Trait;
            if (trait[$internal].type === 'tag') continue; // Skip tags
            traits.push(trait);
            stores.push(getStore(world, trait));
        }
    }
}

export function createEmptyQueryResult(): QueryResult<QueryParameter[]> {
    const results = Object.assign([], {
        readEach: () => results,
        updateEach: () => results,
        useStores: () => results,
        select: () => results,
        sort: () => results,
    }) as QueryResult<QueryParameter[]>;

    return results;
}

// Cached no-op result methods for relation-only queries
const relationOnlyMethods = {
    readEach(this: QueryResult<any>, callback: any) {
        // No traits to read, just iterate entities
        for (let i = 0; i < this.length; i++) {
            callback([], this[i], i);
        }
        return this;
    },
    updateEach(this: QueryResult<any>, callback: any) {
        // No traits to update, just iterate entities
        for (let i = 0; i < this.length; i++) {
            callback([], this[i], i);
        }
        return this;
    },
    useStores(this: QueryResult<any>, callback: any) {
        // No stores, call with empty array
        callback([], this);
        return this;
    },
    select(this: QueryResult<any>) {
        // No-op, nothing to select
        return this;
    },
};

/**
 * Lightweight query result for relation-only queries.
 * Skips store/trait setup since we only need to iterate entities.
 */
export function createRelationOnlyQueryResult<T extends QueryParameter[]>(
    entities: Entity[]
): QueryResult<T> {
    const results = Object.assign(entities, {
        readEach: relationOnlyMethods.readEach,
        updateEach: relationOnlyMethods.updateEach,
        useStores: relationOnlyMethods.useStores,
        select: relationOnlyMethods.select,
        sort(
            callback: (a: Entity, b: Entity) => number = (a, b) => getEntityId(a) - getEntityId(b)
        ): QueryResult<T> {
            Array.prototype.sort.call(entities, callback);
            return results;
        },
    }) as unknown as QueryResult<T>;

    return results;
}

/* @inline */ function getTrackedTraits(
    traits: Trait[],
    world: World,
    query: QueryInstance,
    trackedIndices: number[],

/* @inline */ function createSnapshots(
    world: World,
    entity: Entity,
    traits: Trait[],
    stores: Store<any>[],
    relationPairs: (RelationPair | undefined)[],
    state: any[]
) {
    for (let i = 0; i < traits.length; i++) {
        const trait = traits[i];
        const pair = relationPairs[i];
        const target = pair && typeof pair[$internal].target === 'number' ? pair[$internal].target : undefined;

        if (target !== undefined) {
            const relation = pair![$internal].relation as Relation<Trait>;
            state[i] = getRelationData(world, entity, relation, target);
        } else {
            const ctx = trait[$internal];
            state[i] = ctx.get(getEntityId(entity), stores[i]);
        }
    }
}

/* @inline */ function createSnapshotsWithAtomic(
    world: World,
    entity: Entity,
    traits: Trait[],
    stores: Store<any>[],
    relationPairs: (RelationPair | undefined)[],
    state: any[],
    atomicSnapshots: any[]
) {
    for (let j = 0; j < traits.length; j++) {
        const trait = traits[j];
        const pair = relationPairs[j];
        const target = pair && typeof pair[$internal].target === 'number' ? pair[$internal].target : undefined;

        if (target !== undefined) {
            const relation = pair![$internal].relation as Relation<Trait>;
            const value = getRelationData(world, entity, relation, target);
            state[j] = value;
            atomicSnapshots[j] = trait[$internal].type === 'aos' ? { ...value } : null;
        } else {
            const ctx = trait[$internal];
            const value = ctx.get(getEntityId(entity), stores[j]);
            state[j] = value;
            atomicSnapshots[j] = ctx.type === 'aos' ? { ...value } : null;
        }
    }
}

/* @inline */ function commitPairOrTrait(
    world: World,
    entity: Entity,
    eid: number,
    trait: Trait,
    store: Store<any>,
    pair: RelationPair | undefined,
    newValue: any,
    oldValue: any
): boolean {
    const target = pair && typeof pair[$internal].target === 'number' ? pair[$internal].target : undefined;

    if (target !== undefined) {
        const relation = pair![$internal].relation as Relation<Trait>;
        const previous = getRelationData(world, entity, relation, target);
        const changed = !shallowEqual(previous, newValue);
        if (changed) setRelationData(world, entity, relation, target, newValue);
        return changed;
    }

    const ctx = trait[$internal];
    if (ctx.type === 'aos') {
        const changed = ctx.fastSetWithChangeDetection(eid, store, newValue);
        if (!changed) {
            return !shallowEqual(newValue, oldValue);
        }
        return changed;
    }
    return ctx.fastSetWithChangeDetection(eid, store, newValue);
}

/* @inline */ export function getQueryStores<T extends QueryParameter[]>(
    params: T,
    traits: Trait[],
    stores: Store<any>[],
    relationPairs: (RelationPair | undefined)[],
    world: World
) {
    for (let i = 0; i < params.length; i++) {
        const param = params[i];

        // Handle relation pairs
        if (isRelationPair(param)) {
            const pairCtx = param[$internal];
            const relation = pairCtx.relation as Relation<Trait>;
            const baseTrait = relation[$internal].trait;
            if (baseTrait[$internal].type !== 'tag') {
                traits.push(baseTrait);
                stores.push(getStore(world, baseTrait));
                relationPairs.push(typeof pairCtx.target === 'number' ? param : undefined);
            }
            continue;
        }

        if (isModifier(param)) {
            // Skip not modifier.
            if (param.type === 'not') continue;

            const pairTraits = new Set<number>();
            if (param.pairs) {
                for (const pair of param.pairs) {
                    const pairCtx = pair[$internal];
                    const relation = pairCtx.relation as Relation<Trait>;
                    const baseTrait = relation[$internal].trait;
                    pairTraits.add(baseTrait.id);
                    if (baseTrait[$internal].type === 'tag') continue;

                    traits.push(baseTrait);
                    stores.push(getStore(world, baseTrait));
                    relationPairs.push(typeof pairCtx.target === 'number' ? pair : undefined);
                }
            }

            const modifierTraits = param.traits;
            for (const trait of modifierTraits) {
                if (pairTraits.has(trait.id)) continue; // Already included via pair
                if (trait[$internal].type === 'tag') continue; // Skip tags
                traits.push(trait);
                stores.push(getStore(world, trait));
                relationPairs.push(undefined);
            }
        } else {
            const trait = param as Trait;
            if (trait[$internal].type === 'tag') continue; // Skip tags
            traits.push(trait);
            stores.push(getStore(world, trait));
            relationPairs.push(undefined);
        }
    }
}

export function createEmptyQueryResult(): QueryResult<QueryParameter[]> {
    const results = Object.assign([], {
        readEach: () => results,
        updateEach: () => results,
        useStores: () => results,
        select: () => results,
        sort: () => results,
    }) as QueryResult<QueryParameter[]>;

    return results;
}

// Cached no-op result methods for relation-only queries
const relationOnlyMethods = {
    readEach(this: QueryResult<any>, callback: any) {
        // No traits to read, just iterate entities
        for (let i = 0; i < this.length; i++) {
            callback([], this[i], i);
        }
        return this;
    },
    updateEach(this: QueryResult<any>, callback: any) {
        // No traits to update, just iterate entities
        for (let i = 0; i < this.length; i++) {
            callback([], this[i], i);
        }
        return this;
    },
    useStores(this: QueryResult<any>, callback: any) {
        // No stores, call with empty array
        callback([], this);
        return this;
    },
    select(this: QueryResult<any>) {
        // No-op, nothing to select
        return this;
    },
};

/**
 * Lightweight query result for relation-only queries.
 * Skips store/trait setup since we only need to iterate entities.
 */
export function createRelationOnlyQueryResult<T extends QueryParameter[]>(
    entities: Entity[]
): QueryResult<T> {
    const results = Object.assign(entities, {
        readEach: relationOnlyMethods.readEach,
        updateEach: relationOnlyMethods.updateEach,
        useStores: relationOnlyMethods.useStores,
        select: relationOnlyMethods.select,
        sort(
            callback: (a: Entity, b: Entity) => number = (a, b) => getEntityId(a) - getEntityId(b)
        ): QueryResult<T> {
            Array.prototype.sort.call(entities, callback);
            return results;
        },
    }) as unknown as QueryResult<T>;

    return results;
}

Type errors:

2. Tests: readEach callback destructuring `[contains]` where `InstancesFromParameters` for `Added(Contains(gold))` maybe never because `Contains` is
Relation? `ExtractTraits` returns underlying Trait, but `InstancesFromParameters` for Modifier<TTrait[]> uses `UnwrapModifierData` = Modifier<C> where
C is Trait[]? Wait Modifier generic second type string, `UnwrapModifierData<T> = T extends Modifier<infer C> ? C : never;` For
`Modifier<ExtractTraits<T>, ...>`, C = Trait[]. `InstancesFromParameters<Modifier<C>>` uses `InstancesFromParameters<C>` recursively where C is array
of Traits. That should work. Why never? Maybe type of `Added(Contains(gold))` isn't Modifier due to TS overload inference? Let's inspect types. The
test at line 257 `world.query(Added(Contains(gold))).readEach(([contains], entity) => {` — `InstancesFromParameters<T>` for `[Modifier<Trait[],
string>]` should be `[TraitRecord<Trait>]`. But `TraitRecord` with `Trait<any>` gives unknown maybe. The error says Type 'never' must have iterator,
likely because `Added(Contains(gold))` returns `Modifier<never[], ...>` due to ExtractTraits failing with RelationPair. Our
`ExtractTrait<RelationPair<TPairTrait>>` maybe wrong: `RelationPair<infer TPairTrait>` where `RelationPair<T extends Trait = Trait>`; calling
`Contains(gold)` returns `RelationPair<Trait<Record<string, never>>>`? Actually `Relation<Trait<S>>` returns RelationPair<Trait<S>>. Our ExtractTrait:
```
T extends Relation<infer TTrait> ? TTrait :
T extends RelationPair<infer TPairTrait> ? TPairTrait extends Relation<infer TTrait> ? TTrait : T extends Relation<infer T2> ? T2 : never : T
```
`TPairTrait` is Trait (not Relation), so `TPairTrait extends Relation<...>` false, then `T extends Relation<infer T2>` false, -> never. Oops. Need
ExtractTrait for RelationPair simply return `TPairTrait` because RelationPair's type param is Trait. Let's fix:
```
export type ExtractTrait<T> = T extends Relation<infer TTrait> ? TTrait : T extends RelationPair<infer TPairTrait> ? TPairTrait : T;
```
Let's update.

describe('pair tracking modifiers incremental paths', () => {
    const world = createWorld();
    world.init();

    beforeEach(() => {
        world.reset();
    });

    it('Removed pair works when the query is created before the removal', () => {
        const Likes = relation();
        const apple = world.spawn();
        const banana = world.spawn();
        const player = world.spawn(Likes(apple), Likes(banana));
        const Removed = createRemoved();

        expect(world.query(Removed(Likes(apple)))).toHaveLength(0);

        player.remove(Likes(apple));

        expect(world.query(Removed(Likes(apple)))).toContain(player);
    });

    it('Changed pair works when the query is created before the change', () => {
        const Likes = relation({ store: { amount: 0 } });
        const parent = world.spawn();
        const child = world.spawn(Likes(parent));
        const Changed = createChanged();

        expect(world.query(Changed(Likes(parent)))).toHaveLength(0);

        child.set(Likes(parent), { amount: 2 });

        expect(world.query(Changed(Likes(parent)))).toContain(child);
    });

    it('exclusive replacement works when queries are created before replacement', () => {
        const Targeting = relation({ exclusive: true });
        const oldTarget = world.spawn();
        const newTarget = world.spawn();
        const goblin = world.spawn(Targeting(oldTarget));
        const Added = createAdded();
        const Removed = createRemoved();

        expect(world.query(Added(Targeting(newTarget)))).toHaveLength(0);
        expect(world.query(Removed(Targeting(oldTarget)))).toHaveLength(0);

        goblin.add(Targeting(newTarget));

        expect(world.query(Added(Targeting(newTarget)))).toContain(goblin);
        expect(world.query(Removed(Targeting(oldTarget)))).toContain(goblin);
    });

    it('cancellation works when queries are created before opposite events', () => {
        const Added = createAdded();
        const Removed = createRemoved();
        const ChildOf = relation();
        const parent = world.spawn();
        const child = world.spawn();

        expect(world.query(Added(ChildOf(parent)))).toHaveLength(0);
        expect(world.query(Removed(ChildOf(parent)))).toHaveLength(0);

        child.add(ChildOf(parent));
        child.remove(ChildOf(parent));

        expect(world.query(Added(ChildOf(parent)))).toHaveLength(0);
        expect(world.query(Removed(ChildOf(parent)))).toHaveLength(0);
    });

    it('destruction works when query is created before destruction', () => {
        const Likes = relation();
        const target = world.spawn();
        const entity = world.spawn(Likes(target));
        const Removed = createRemoved();

        expect(world.query(Removed(Likes(target)))).toHaveLength(0);

        entity.destroy();

        expect(world.query(Removed(Likes(target)))).toContain(entity);
    });
});

Cancellation incremental fails: after query created before add/remove, `world.query(Added(...))` returns entity. Let's trace.

Query A `Added(ChildOf(parent))` created before events. Query B `Removed(...)` created before events too (two separate queries). Then child.add ->
addRelationTarget: markPairEvent adds; updateQueriesForRelationPairChange iterates trackingQueries:
- Query A: checkTracking with event add target parent. Group pair add matches -> tracker bit set -> query.add(child).
- Query B: checkTracking event add target parent, group remove/change -> returns false -> query.remove(child).
Then child.remove -> removeRelationTarget: markPairEvent cancels added -> removed remains empty. updateQueriesForRelationPairChange:
- Query A: checkTracking event remove target parent. group type add -> cross-event invalidation returns false -> query.remove(child). Good, should
remove from query A.
- Query B: checkTracking event remove target parent. group type remove; affected true; groupType===eventType -> set tracker bit for remove. Then
satisfaction: tracker bit set -> returns true -> query.add(child) !!! This is the bug: `checkQueryTracking` on the remove event sets tracker bit even
though the remove event canceled an add (event state says no removal). We need cancellation at tracker level: if markPairEvent canceled (i.e., this
event is an opposite event), then query.checkTracking should not record it, and should remove entity from matching queries. How to know? The
`markPairEvent` function currently doesn't return whether cancellation occurred. We can make it return `true` if the event was canceled (opposite),
and `updateQueriesForRelationPairChange` can handle: if canceled, we need to invalidate both added/removed groups and remove entity. But
checkQueryTracking with event type remove on group remove will set tracker, so we need a way to tell it to not set tracker for canceled event.

Options:
- Have `markPairEvent` return `'cancel' | 'record'` and if cancel, call `updateQueriesForRelationPairChange` with a special "cancel" event type? Add
event type `'cancel'`? Could extend checkQueryTracking to accept eventType `'cancel'` meaning don't set tracker, just invalidate matching add/remove
groups and remove entity.
- Simpler: in `updateQueriesForRelationPairChange`, before calling checkTracking, check whether this pair event is still present in event state. If
event type add and pair not in added set (because canceled), then it's a cancellation; call query.checkTracking with eventType 'remove'? That would
invalidate Added but also set Removed tracker (wrong). Need a cancel event.

Let's add `'cancel'` to EventType internal? It's used widely. Could extend `EventType` to include `'cancel'` but that may affect other code.
Alternatively, in `checkQueryTracking`, add a parameter `pairCanceled?: boolean` and when true, for pair groups:
- Do not set tracker bit.
- Perform cross-event invalidation: if eventType==='add' and groupType remove/change -> return false; if eventType==='remove' and groupType add/change
-> return false.
- Also for groupType matching eventType (e.g., remove event and group remove), we should return false? Since cancellation means no remove event should
be recorded. For a Removed group, returning false removes entity from query (which is already not in query for remove? Actually after add, Query B not
in query; on cancel remove, Query B should remain out). So just don't set tracker; then satisfaction check for group remove: tracker not set ->
returns false (good).
- For Added group on cancel remove: cross-event invalidation returns false (removes entity, already out).
So implement `checkQueryTracking` with optional `pairCanceled` flag. When `affected` and `pairCanceled`:
  - Skip tracker update and skip cross-event invalidation? Wait for Added group on cancel remove, we DO want to invalidate Added group to ensure
entity removed. But if entity already not in query? It was added by previous add event; query A contains child. On remove cancel, we need remove it.
Cross-event invalidation with eventType remove on group add returns false -> query.remove. Good.
  - For Removed group on cancel remove, if we return false (without setting tracker), query B remains out. So for cancel remove, we should not set
tracker and also not set groupType===eventType branch; but cross-event invalidation for groupType add/change should still happen. So:
```
if (pairCanceled) {
  // only cross-invalidate opposite groups
  if (eventType === 'remove') {
     if (groupType === 'add' || groupType === 'change') return false;
  } else if (eventType === 'add') {
     if (groupType === 'remove' || groupType === 'change') return false;
  }
  // skip tracker update
} else { normal }
```
But for cancel remove, groupType remove should not invalidate; it just stays unsatisfied (return false later). Good.
For cancel add (remove then add), eventType add: group remove/change return false; group add should not set tracker, remains unsatisfied (query A
stays out). Good.

Need know `pairCanceled`. Modify `markPairEvent` to return boolean `true` if event canceled (i.e., removed an opposite entry), `false` if recorded.
For change always false.

        // Check required traits
        if (required && (entityMask & required) !== required) return false;

        // Check Or traits
        if (or !== 0 && (entityMask & or) === 0) return false;
    }

    // 2. Process tracking groups - update trackers and check cross-event invalidation
    // Also track OR group state to avoid second loop when possible
    let hasOrGroup = false;
    let anyOrMatched = false;

    for (let i = 0; i < trackingGroupsLen; i++) {
        const group = trackingGroups[i];
        const groupType = group.type;
        const groupLogic = group.logic;
        const groupBitmasks = group.bitmasks;
        const groupBitmask = groupBitmasks[eventGenerationId];

        // Determine whether this event affects this group. Pair groups are only
        // affected when the incoming target matches their tracked pair.
        let affected = !!(groupBitmask && (groupBitmask & eventBitflag));
        if (affected && group.pairs && group.pairs.length > 0) {
            const pair = group.pairs[0];
            const pairCtx = pair[$internal];
            const pairRelationTrait = pairCtx.relation[$internal].trait;
            const pairInstance = getTraitInstance(world[$internal].traitInstances, pairRelationTrait);
            const pairGeneration = pairInstance?.generationId;
            const pairBitflag = pairInstance?.bitflag;

            const eventIsPairTrait =
                pairGeneration === eventGenerationId && pairBitflag === eventBitflag;

            if (!eventIsPairTrait) {
                // Regular trait event: pair group unaffected.
                affected = false;
            } else {
                const pairTarget = pairCtx.target;
                if (pairTarget !== '*' && target !== pairTarget) {
                    affected = false;
                }
            }
        }

        if (affected) {
            // Cross-event invalidation:
            // - Remove event invalidates Added/Changed tracking
            // - Add event invalidates Removed/Changed tracking
            if (eventType === 'remove') {
                if (groupType === 'add' || groupType === 'change') return false;
            } else if (eventType === 'add') {
                if (groupType === 'remove' || groupType === 'change') return false;
            }

            // A cancelled opposite pair event must not record a new tracker bit.
            if (pairCanceled) {
                // Fall through to satisfaction check: the group remains unsatisfied.
            } else if (groupType === eventType) {
                // For change events, verify entity still has the trait / pair
                if (eventType === 'change') {
                    if (group.pairs && group.pairs.length > 0) {
                        if (!hasRelationPair(world, entity, group.pairs[0])) return false;
                    } else {
                        const genMasks = entityMasks[eventGenerationId];
                        const entityMask = genMasks ? (genMasks[eid] | 0) : 0;
                        if (!(entityMask & eventBitflag)) return false;
                    }
                }

                // PERF: Cache tracker array reference before mutation
                const groupTrackers = group.trackers;
                let trackerArr = groupTrackers[eventGenerationId];
                if (!trackerArr) {
                    trackerArr = [];
                    groupTrackers[eventGenerationId] = trackerArr;
                }
                trackerArr[eid] = (trackerArr[eid] | 0) | eventBitflag;
            }
        }

start=s.index("export function markPairEvent(")

old=s[start:end]
new='''export function markPairEvent(
    world: World,
    relationTrait: Trait,
    entity: Entity,
    target: Entity,
    type: 'add' | 'remove' | 'change'
): Map<number, boolean> {
    const ctx = world[$internal];
    const traitId = relationTrait.id;
    const canceledByTracker = new Map<number, boolean>();

    for (const [trackerId, tracker] of ctx.relationTrackers) {
        const eventMap =
            type === 'add'
                ? tracker.added
                : type === 'remove'
                  ? tracker.removed
                  : tracker.changed;

        let byEntity = eventMap.get(traitId);
        if (!byEntity) {
            byEntity = new Map();
            eventMap.set(traitId, byEntity);
        }

        let targets = byEntity.get(entity);
        if (!targets) {
            targets = new Set();
            byEntity.set(entity, targets);
        }

        let canceled = false;

        if (type === 'add') {
            const removedByEntity = tracker.removed.get(traitId);
            const removedTargets = removedByEntity?.get(entity);
            if (removedTargets?.delete(target)) {
                canceled = true;
                if (removedTargets.size === 0) removedByEntity!.delete(entity);
            } else {
                targets.add(target);
            }
        } else if (type === 'remove') {
            const addedByEntity = tracker.added.get(traitId);
            const addedTargets = addedByEntity?.get(entity);
            if (addedTargets?.delete(target)) {
                canceled = true;
                if (addedTargets.size === 0) addedByEntity!.delete(entity);
            } else {
                targets.add(target);
            }
        } else {
            targets.add(target);
        }

        canceledByTracker.set(trackerId, canceled);
    }

    return canceledByTracker;
}

'''

import { $internal } from '../common';
import type { Entity } from '../entity/types';
import { getEntityId } from '../entity/utils/pack-entity';
import { getTraitInstance } from '../trait/trait-instance';
import type { Trait } from '../trait/types';
import type { World } from '../world';

/** Per-modifier relation pair tracking state. */
export type RelationTracker = {
    /** Initial pairs at factory creation / world reset: relationTraitId -> source -> targets */
    snapshot: Map<number, Map<number, Set<number>>>;
    /** Uncancelled pair additions within observation window */
    added: Map<number, Map<number, Set<number>>>;
    /** Uncancelled pair removals within observation window */
    removed: Map<number, Map<number, Set<number>>>;
    /** Pair changes within observation window */
    changed: Map<number, Map<number, Set<number>>>;
};

export function createRelationTracker(): RelationTracker {
    return {
        snapshot: new Map(),
        added: new Map(),
        removed: new Map(),
        changed: new Map(),
    };
}

/**
 * Record a pair-level event. Opposite add/remove events on the same target cancel.
 * Returns a map from tracking modifier id to whether that modifier's event was cancelled.
 */
export function markPairEvent(
    world: World,
    relationTrait: Trait,
    entity: Entity,
    target: Entity,
    type: 'add' | 'remove' | 'change'
): Map<number, boolean> {
    const ctx = world[$internal];
    const traitId = relationTrait.id;
    const canceledByTracker = new Map<number, boolean>();

    for (const [trackerId, tracker] of ctx.relationTrackers) {
        const eventMap =
            type === 'add'
                ? tracker.added
                : type === 'remove'
                  ? tracker.removed
                  : tracker.changed;

        let byEntity = eventMap.get(traitId);
        if (!byEntity) {
            byEntity = new Map();
            eventMap.set(traitId, byEntity);
        }

        let targets = byEntity.get(entity);
        if (!targets) {
            targets = new Set();
            byEntity.set(entity, targets);
        }

        let canceled = false;

        if (type === 'add') {
            const removedByEntity = tracker.removed.get(traitId);
            const removedTargets = removedByEntity?.get(entity);
            if (removedTargets?.delete(target)) {
                canceled = true;
                if (removedTargets.size === 0) removedByEntity!.delete(entity);
            } else {
                targets.add(target);
            }
        } else if (type === 'remove') {
            const addedByEntity = tracker.added.get(traitId);
            const addedTargets = addedByEntity?.get(entity);
            if (addedTargets?.delete(target)) {
                canceled = true;
                if (addedTargets.size === 0) addedByEntity!.delete(entity);
            } else {
                targets.add(target);
            }
        } else {
            targets.add(target);
        }

        canceledByTracker.set(trackerId, canceled);
    }

    return canceledByTracker;
}

/**
 * Update tracking queries that reference the relation trait after a pair-level event.
 */
export function updateQueriesForRelationPairChange(
    world: World,
    relationTrait: Trait,
    entity: Entity,
    target: Entity,
    eventType: 'add' | 'remove' | 'change',
    canceledByTracker?: Map<number, boolean>
) {
    const ctx = world[$internal];
    const instance = getTraitInstance(ctx.traitInstances, relationTrait);
    if (!instance) return;

    const { generationId, bitflag } = instance;

    for (const query of instance.trackingQueries) {
        const match = query.checkTracking(
            world,
            entity,
            eventType,
            generationId,
            bitflag,
            target,
            canceledByTracker
        );
        if (match) query.add(entity);
        else query.remove(world, entity);
    }
}

/** Get a nested map by relation trait id. */
function getTargetSet(
    map: Map<number, Map<number, Set<number>>>,
    traitId: number,
    entity: Entity
): Set<number> | undefined {
    return map.get(traitId)?.get(entity);
}

/** Check if a specific pair is present in a pair event map. */
export function hasPairEvent(
    world: World,
    trackerId: number,
    relationTrait: Trait,
    entity: Entity,
    target: Entity | '*',
    type: 'add' | 'remove' | 'change'
): boolean {
    const tracker = world[$internal].relationTrackers.get(trackerId);
    if (!tracker) return false;

    const map =
        type === 'add'
            ? tracker.added
            : type === 'remove'
              ? tracker.removed
              : tracker.changed;

    const targets = getTargetSet(map, relationTrait.id, entity);
    if (!targets) return false;
    if (target === '*') return targets.size > 0;
    return targets.has(target);
}

/** Check if a specific pair existed in the initial snapshot. */
export function hasPairSnapshot(
    world: World,
    trackerId: number,
    relationTrait: Trait,
    entity: Entity,
    target: Entity | '*'
): boolean {
    const tracker = world[$internal].relationTrackers.get(trackerId);
    if (!tracker) return false;
    const targets = getTargetSet(tracker.snapshot, relationTrait.id, entity);
    if (!targets) return false;
    if (target === '*') return targets.size > 0;
    return targets.has(target);
}

/** Build the pair snapshot for a tracker from current world state. */
export function populateRelationTrackerSnapshot(world: World, tracker: RelationTracker) {
    const ctx = world[$internal];
    for (const relation of ctx.relations) {
        const relationTrait = relation[$internal].trait;
        const instance = getTraitInstance(ctx.traitInstances, relationTrait);
        if (!instance || !instance.relationTargets) continue;

        const byEntity = new Map<number, Set<number>>();
        tracker.snapshot.set(relationTrait.id, byEntity);

        const targets = instance.relationTargets;
        for (let eid = 0; eid < targets.length; eid++) {
            const relationCtx = relation[$internal];
            let entityTargets: number[] | undefined;
            if (relationCtx.exclusive) {
                const t = (targets as Array<number | undefined>)[eid];
                if (t !== undefined) entityTargets = [t];
            } else {
                entityTargets = (targets as number[][])[eid];
            }
            if (!entityTargets || entityTargets.length === 0) continue;

            // The entity index dense array holds the packed entity for each eid.
            const denseIdx = ctx.entityIndex.sparse[eid];
            const packedEntity = ctx.entityIndex.dense[denseIdx];
            if (packedEntity === undefined || getEntityId(packedEntity) !== eid) continue;

            byEntity.set(packedEntity, new Set(entityTargets));
        }
    }
}

REASONING_CONTENT
Now clear: On remove, query A (Added group id 3) CQ logs `ev remove gt add gid 3 canceled true target 1`, then returns false (cross invalidation) so
`query.remove` should be called. But q len 1 after query. Why? Let's inspect `query.remove` path. It does:
```
removeEntityFromQuery(world, query, entity) {
  if (!query.entities.has(entity) || query.toRemove.has(entity)) return;
  query.toRemove.add(entity);
  ctx.dirtyQueries.add(query);
  ...
}
```
Then `runQuery` calls `commitQueryRemovals`, which iterates `ctx.dirtyQueries`, removes toRemove. Should work.

But wait: there are TWO queries? In debug test, we only created Added query before events. We did not create Removed query? Actually we did
`world.query(Added(...))` and `world.query(Removed(...))` before events. Yes two queries. On add, query A added child. On remove, updateQueries for
query A: checkTracking returns false -> `query.remove(world, entity)`. But `removeEntityFromQuery` only adds to `toRemove` if
`query.entities.has(entity)`. It should. Then `commitQueryRemovals` in runQuery should remove. But log shows q len 1.

Maybe the issue is that on remove, `updateQueriesForRelationPairChange` is called BEFORE `removeRelationTarget` actually removes the relation from
entity? Let's look at removeRelationTarget: it mutates relationTargets (removes target), then calls markPairEvent and updateQueries. At that point
relation removed. checkQueryTracking for Added group with eventType remove, canceled true returns false. query.remove. Good.

But then after removeRelationTarget returns, `removeRelationPair` continues. Since wasLastTarget true (only pair), it calls `removeTraitFromEntity`.
That path also loops `trackingQueries` for relation trait and calls `checkQueryTracking` (without target) with eventType remove. For query A (Added
pair), in checkQueryTracking: affected true (group has bit), but group.pairs exists, target undefined, pairTarget parent => affected=false. So no
cross invalidation, no tracker update. Then satisfaction check: group tracker still has bit (from add) -> returns true! So query.add(entity) re-adds
child! That's the bug. The trait-level removal path doesn't know target, so it doesn't invalidate the pair group. But it should remove the entity
because the pair no longer exists. More generally, when a trait-level remove happens and the query has pair groups, those pair groups should be
invalidated even without target because the whole relation trait is being removed (which means all pairs removed). For Added/Changed pair groups, if
base trait removed, any tracked pair add should be invalidated. For Removed pair groups, trait-level removal of base trait means all active pairs
removed; we need to record Removed for each pair? But that's handled by pair event update before removeTraitFromEntity. However trait-level remove
path then re-adds via Added group because tracker remains.

We need `checkQueryTracking` when called with target undefined (trait-level event) to treat pair groups appropriately:
- If event is for the pair's relation trait and target undefined (i.e., trait-level add/remove of base trait), what should happen?
  - On `remove` of base trait: all pair groups for that trait should be invalidated (Added/Changed) and Removed groups should have their tracker set?
But pair-level remove event already set Removed tracker before trait remove. The trait-level remove path should not overwrite.
  - On `add` of base trait (first add): pair-level add event already set Added tracker; trait-level add path should not mess.
So for pair groups when event is for pair trait and target undefined, we should treat as affected for cross-event invalidation? But we also need to
avoid setting tracker for the same event (since pair event already did). If we treat affected with target undefined:
  - For Added group on trait remove: cross invalidate -> return false (removes). Good.
  - For Removed group on trait remove: groupType remove and eventType remove; if we set tracker, that's okay? But pair event already set it; duplicate
set fine. But for canceled removals (e.g., pair removed but canceled), trait-level remove might re-set tracker incorrectly. In cancellation scenario,
after pair add+remove, base trait was removed (last target). Pair event update removed Added and kept Removed out. Then trait-level remove path if it
sets Removed tracker would re-add Removed query (wrong). So we must NOT set tracker in trait-level path for pair groups; only cross-invalidate.
  - For Changed group on trait remove: cross invalidate -> false.
  - For trait-level add: should we set tracker for pair groups? Pair event already did. If we also set, duplicate fine. But for a query where pair
group exists and first add happens, pair event sets tracker; trait add path setting again fine. For removed->add cancellation, pair event add is
canceled and does NOT set tracker; trait add path would set tracker incorrectly. So do not set tracker in trait-level path for pair groups; only
cross-invalidate on remove.

So modify checkQueryTracking: when group.pairs and target undefined (or target mismatch?) but event trait matches pair trait:
- For trait-level event (target undefined), treat as affected for cross-event invalidation only:
  - if eventType remove and groupType add/change -> return false.
  - if eventType add and groupType remove/change -> return false.
  - do NOT update tracker.
- Do not require target match.

But we also need handle trait-level add for Removed group: cross invalidate -> false, which is correct (an add of base trait cancels any remove
tracking for all pairs? Actually if entity removed all pairs then re-added base trait with new target, Removed query for old target should remain? Hmm
complex. Pair events handle per-target; trait-level add path would invalidate Removed groups broadly, which could incorrectly remove a Removed(old)
event when a new pair added. But in `addRelationPair`, pair event update happens after `addTraitToEntity`? Let's trace order in `addRelationPair`:
1. If first add: `addTraitToEntity` -> trait-level add update happens FIRST (before addRelationTarget). At that point no pair added yet. Then
`addRelationTarget` -> pair add event.
So trait-level add path for Removed groups happens before new pair exists. If entity previously removed old pair and now adding new pair (not old),
Removed(old) should still match. But trait-level add path with no target would cross-invalidate all Removed groups, removing Removed(old) incorrectly.
Hmm.

Maybe we shouldn't cross-invalidate pair groups on trait-level events at all; instead, pair-level events handle everything. But then cancellation
case's Added query would remain because trait-level remove doesn't invalidate. However pair-level remove event already invalidates Added before
trait-level remove. The re-add by trait-level remove path is the problem; we could simply prevent trait-level path from adding pair group queries when
target undefined, i.e., make `checkQueryTracking` return false for pair groups when target undefined? But that would remove entity from query during
trait-level remove (good) and not add during trait-level add (pair event will add later). What about trait-level add for Removed group: if target
undefined, we don't want to invalidate Removed(old) when adding new pair. But `addTraitToEntity` happens before new pair exists, and query for
Removed(old) might have entity in query from previous remove event. If checkQueryTracking returns false for pair group when target undefined, it would
remove entity from Removed(old) query during any trait-level add. That's bad.

We need more nuanced: trait-level event should NOT affect pair groups at all, because pair-level events handle them. The problem is trait-level remove
path currently RE-ADDS entity because it evaluates group satisfaction with stale tracker. If we simply skip pair groups entirely in
`checkQueryTracking` when target is undefined (both update and satisfaction? No, we still need satisfaction for overall query when events for other
traits happen), then trait-level remove path would not re-add because pair group satisfaction not checked? Actually if we skip the group in
satisfaction, query might remain in entities due to other groups. For a query with only pair group, skipping satisfaction would return true (no groups
checked), causing query.add. So can't skip satisfaction.

Better: for trait-level event with target undefined and group.pairs, we should:
- Not update tracker.
- For satisfaction check, pair group's tracker should be considered, but if the trait-level event is a remove and the entity no longer has the base
trait, then the pair no longer exists, so the Added/Changed tracker should be treated as unsatisfied regardless of tracker bit. For Removed groups,
tracker state from pair event should remain.

So in satisfaction check for pair groups, if eventType is remove and target undefined and groupType is add/change and the base trait no longer exists
(or simply because trait remove event), return false (invalidate). For Removed groups, keep tracker as-is. For eventType add and target undefined and
groupType remove/change, should we invalidate? As argued, first add occurs before new pair added, so a Removed(old) query should NOT be invalidated by
adding a different pair. But if the same entity had no base trait and now adds a pair, pair-level add event will handle cancellation per target.
Trait-level add shouldn't invalidate Removed groups. So for eventType add, do nothing for pair groups in trait-level path.

Thus minimal fix for cancellation: In `checkQueryTracking`, when `affected` and group.pairs and target === undefined:
- If eventType === 'remove' && (groupType === 'add' || groupType === 'change'): return false (cross-invalidate because base trait removal invalidates
pair additions/changes).
- Otherwise, do not update tracker (fall through).
- Also for change events without target (markChanged trait-level, e.g., regular relation data change), don't affect pair groups.

Let's implement this. Currently code:
```
if (affected && group.pairs...) {
  if (!eventIsPairTrait) affected=false;
  else { if pairTarget !== '*' && target !== pairTarget) affected=false; }
}
```
We'll modify:
```
if (affected && group.pairs...) {
  const eventIsPairTrait = ...
  if (!eventIsPairTrait) affected=false;
  else if (target === undefined) {
     // Trait-level structural event. Only cross-invalidate add/change on remove.
     affected = true;
     // We'll handle below: pairCanceled should not apply; tracker should not be updated.
  } else {
     if (pairTarget !== '*' && target !== pairTarget) affected=false;
  }
}
```
Then in affected block:
- If target undefined and group.pairs:
  - if eventType remove and (groupType add||change) return false;
  - skip tracker update (like pairCanceled true) but don't set pairCanceled from map.
  - fall through satisfaction.
This should remove Added query on trait remove. For Removed group on trait remove, satisfaction tracker set by pair event remains -> true (query.add,
but it's already in query? Actually Removed query was not in query after add event; pair remove event adds it before trait remove; then trait remove

tracker set from pair event -> true -> query.add (already true, no-op). Good. For canceled scenario, Removed tracker not set (pair remove canceled),
trait remove path doesn't set -> false -> stays out. Great.

What about Added query after pair add then trait remove: pair remove event (canceled true) already invalidates Added and removes. Then trait remove
path returns false too; no re-add. Good.

describe('pair tracking modifiers edge cases', () => {
    const world = createWorld();
    world.init();

    beforeEach(() => {
        world.reset();
    });

    it('destruction fires pair-level removal for every active pair', () => {
        const Likes = relation();
        const targetA = world.spawn();
        const targetB = world.spawn();
        const entity = world.spawn(Likes(targetA), Likes(targetB));
        const Removed = createRemoved();

        entity.destroy();

        expect(world.query(Removed(Likes(targetA)))).toContain(entity);
        expect(world.query(Removed(Likes(targetB)))).toContain(entity);
    });

    it('wildcard removed matches any removed pair', () => {
        const Likes = relation();
        const targetA = world.spawn();
        const targetB = world.spawn();
        const entityA = world.spawn(Likes(targetA));
        const entityB = world.spawn(Likes(targetB));
        const Removed = createRemoved();

        entityA.remove(Likes(targetA));
        entityB.remove(Likes(targetB));

        const removed = world.query(Removed(Likes('*')));
        expect(removed).toContain(entityA);
        expect(removed).toContain(entityB);
    });

    it('Or composes pair modifiers with regular tracking modifiers', () => {
        const Added = createAdded();
        const Likes = relation();
        const Foo = trait();
        const target = world.spawn();
        const entityA = world.spawn();
        const entityB = world.spawn();

        entityA.add(Likes(target));
        entityB.add(Foo);

        const entities = world.query(Or(Added(Likes(target)), Added(Foo)));
        expect(entities).toContain(entityA);
        expect(entities).toContain(entityB);
    });

    it('pair query created after events is populated from accumulated state', () => {
        const Added = createAdded();
        const Likes = relation();
        const target = world.spawn();
        const entity = world.spawn();
        entity.add(Likes(target));

        // First query drains the event.
        expect(world.query(Added(Likes(target)))).toContain(entity);
        // A second query has no new events.
        expect(world.query(Added(Likes(target)))).toHaveLength(0);

        const targetB = world.spawn();
        const entityB = world.spawn();
        entityB.add(Likes(targetB));
        expect(world.query(Added(Likes(targetB)))).toContain(entityB);
    });
});

REASONING_CONTENT
Potential issue: In `checkQueryTrackingAtCreation`, for trait-level `Changed` groups we use `changedMask` which is never cleared; okay. For pair
groups, `hasPairEvent` reads `ctx.relationTrackers.get(trackerId)`. But tracker id is modifier factory id. Good.

Potential issue: `query.traitInstances.all` includes duplicate instances (from pair groups and regular groups) if same trait appears in multiple
groups. `checkQuery` static constraints use required/forbidden/or only, not all. `checkQueryTracking` early exit `if (traitInstancesAll.length === 0)
return false;` fine. But `query.generations` dedupes. No functional issue.

In query/types.ts:

export type InstancesFromParameters<T> = ... First extends Modifier
   ? IsNotModifier<First> extends true ? [] :
     First extends OrModifier<infer Params> ? InstancesFromParameters<Params> : InstancesFromParameters<UnwrapModifierData<First>>
```
But OrModifier's `modifiers` is `Modifier[]` (not parameterized by T?). `OrModifier<T extends OrParameter[]> = Modifier<...> & { modifiers: Modifier[]
}` loses type info. Could change OrModifier to keep modifiers typed `T`? Let's inspect Or type:
```
export type OrModifier<T extends OrParameter[] = OrParameter[]> = Modifier<ExtractTraitsFromOrParams<T>, 'or'> & { modifiers: Modifier[] };
```
It stores `modifiers: Modifier[]` (untyped). Could change to `modifiers: T`? But runtime modifiers array includes Modifier objects, T includes Trait |

type ExtractModifiers<T> = T extends [infer F, ...infer R] ? (F extends Modifier ? [F, ...ExtractModifiers<R>] : ExtractModifiers<R>) : []
type ExtractTraitsFromOrParams...
type OrModifier<T extends OrParameter[]> = Modifier<ExtractTraitsFromOrParams<T>, 'or'> & { modifiers: ExtractModifiers<T> };
```
Then `Or` factory can return `OrModifier<T>` where T is params. But runtime `modifiers` array currently pushes Modifier objects. Type mapping works.

        const Likes = relation();

        const target = world.spawn();
        const withFoo = world.spawn(Foo);
        const withoutFoo = world.spawn();

        withFoo.add(Likes(target));
        withoutFoo.add(Likes(target));

        expect(entities).toContain(withFoo);
        expect(entities).not.toContain(withoutFoo);

        const target = world.spawn();
        const source = world.spawn(Likes(target));
        const Removed = createRemoved();

## Tracking modifiers

Track structural and data changes. Each tracking modifier must be created as a unique instance.

```typescript
import { createAdded, createRemoved, createChanged } from 'koota'

// Create unique instances (typically at module scope)
const Added = createAdded()
const Removed = createRemoved()
const Changed = createChanged()
```

**Added** - Entities that added a trait since last query:

```typescript
const newPositions = world.query(Added(Position))

// Track relation additions
const newChildren = world.query(Added(ChildOf))
```

**Removed** - Entities that removed a trait since last query (includes destroyed entities):

```typescript
const stoppedEntities = world.query(Removed(Velocity))

// Track orphaned entities
const orphaned = world.query(Removed(ChildOf))
```

**Changed** - Entities whose trait data changed since last query:

```typescript
const movedEntities = world.query(Changed(Position))

// Track relation data changes
const updatedChildren = world.query(Changed(ChildOf))
```

**Logical AND (default):**

When multiple traits are passed to a tracking modifier, it uses logical AND. Only entities where **all** specified traits match the condition are returned:

```typescript
// Entities where BOTH Position AND Velocity were added
const fullyAdded = world.query(Added(Position, Velocity))

// Entities where BOTH Position AND Velocity were removed
const fullyRemoved = world.query(Removed(Position, Velocity))

// Entities where BOTH Position AND Velocity have changed
const fullyUpdated = world.query(Changed(Position, Velocity))
---relations---
# Relations

Relations build graphs between entities. Use for hierarchies, inventories, targeting, neighbor networks, and any entity-to-entity connection.

## Contents

- [Core Concepts](#core-concepts)
- [Basic Syntax](#basic-syntax)
- [Building Graphs](#building-graphs) - Hierarchies, inventories, targeting, neighbors
- [Querying Relations](#querying-relations) - Specific targets, wildcards, combined queries
- [Traversing Graphs](#traversing-graphs) - Recursive traversal, building trees, finding ancestors
- [Ordered Relations](#ordered-relations) - Maintaining order (experimental)
- [Removing Relations](#removing-relations)
- [Relation Options](#relation-options)
- [React Hooks](#react-hooks)
- [Anti-Patterns](#anti-patterns) - Common mistakes to avoid

## Core Concepts

A relation connects a **source** entity to a **target** entity. The source owns the relation.

```
┌─────────┐  ChildOf(Parent)  ┌─────────┐
│  Child  │ ─────────────────▶│ Parent  │
│ (source)│                   │ (target)│
└─────────┘                   └─────────┘
```

The child expresses the relationship, not the parent. This enables efficient batch queries for all children of a parent.

## Basic Syntax

```typescript
import { relation } from 'koota'

// Basic relation (no data)
const ChildOf = relation()

// Relation with data
const Contains = relation({ store: { amount: 0 } })

// Auto cleanup when target destroyed
const ChildOf = relation({ autoDestroy: 'orphan' })

// Only one target allowed per entity
const Targeting = relation({ exclusive: true })
```

## Building Graphs

### Hierarchies (parent-child)

```typescript
const ChildOf = relation({ autoDestroy: 'orphan' })

const parent = world.spawn()
const child = world.spawn(ChildOf(parent))
const grandchild = world.spawn(ChildOf(child))

// Destroying parent destroys entire subtree
parent.destroy() // child and grandchild also destroyed
```

### Inventories (contains)

```typescript
const Contains = relation({ store: { amount: 0 } })

const inventory = world.spawn()
const gold = world.spawn()
const sword = world.spawn()

inventory.add(Contains(gold, { amount: 100 }))
inventory.add(Contains(sword, { amount: 1 }))

// Update amount
inventory.set(Contains(gold), { amount: 50 })

// Read amount
const data = inventory.get(Contains(gold)) // { amount: 50 }
```

### Targeting/Following

```typescript
const Targeting = relation({ exclusive: true })

const enemy = world.spawn()
const player = world.spawn()
const otherPlayer = world.spawn()

enemy.add(Targeting(player))
enemy.add(Targeting(otherPlayer)) // Replaces previous target

enemy.has(Targeting(player)) // false
enemy.has(Targeting(otherPlayer)) // true
```

### Neighbor Networks

```typescript
const NeighborOf = relation()

// Build bidirectional connections
entityA.add(NeighborOf(entityB))
entityB.add(NeighborOf(entityA))
```

## Querying Relations

### Query children of specific parent

```typescript
const children = world.query(ChildOf(parent))

for (const child of children) {
  // Process each child
}
```

### Query all entities with any relation (wildcard)

```typescript
// All entities that are children of something
const allChildren = world.query(ChildOf('*'))

// All entities that contain something
const allContainers = world.query(Contains('*'))
```

### Get targets from an entity

```typescript
// Get all targets
const items = entity.targetsFor(Contains) // Entity[]

// Get first target
const target = entity.targetFor(Targeting) // Entity | undefined
```

### Combined queries

```typescript
// Enemies targeting the player
const threats = world.query(IsEnemy, Targeting(player))

// Children of parent that also have Position
const positionedChildren = world.query(ChildOf(parent), Position)
```

  const children = world.query(ChildOf(node))
  for (const child of children) {

import type { Schema } from './types';

function createSoASetFunction(schema: Schema) {
    const keys = Object.keys(schema);

    // Generate a hardcoded set function based on the schema keys
    const setFunctionBody = keys
        .map((key) => `if ('${key}' in value) store.${key}[index] = value.${key};`)
        .join('\n    ');

    // Use new Function to create a set function with hardcoded keys
    const set = new Function(
        'index',
        'store',
        'value',
        `
		${setFunctionBody}
	  `
    );

    return set;
}

function createSoAFastSetFunction(schema: Schema) {
    const keys = Object.keys(schema);

    // Generate a hardcoded set function based on the schema keys
    const setFunctionBody = keys.map((key) => `store.${key}[index] = value.${key};`).join('\n    ');

    // Use new Function to create a set function with hardcoded keys
    const set = new Function(
        'index',
        'store',
        'value',
        `
		${setFunctionBody}
	  `
    );

    return set;
}

// Return true if any trait value were changed.
function createSoAFastSetChangeFunction(schema: Schema) {
    const keys = Object.keys(schema);

    // Generate a hardcoded set function based on the schema keys
    const setFunctionBody = keys
        .map(
            (key) =>
                `if (store.${key}[index] !== value.${key}) {
            store.${key}[index] = value.${key};
            changed = true;
        }`
        )
        .join('\n    ');

    // Use new Function to create a set function with hardcoded keys
    const set = new Function(
        'index',
        'store',
        'value',
        `
        let changed = false;
        ${setFunctionBody}
        return changed;
        `
    );

    return set;
}

function createSoAGetFunction(schema: Schema) {
    const keys = Object.keys(schema);

    // Create an object literal with all keys assigned from the store
    const objectLiteral = `{ ${keys.map((key) => `${key}: store.${key}[index]`).join(', ')} }`;

    // Use new Function to create a get function that returns the pre-populated object
    const get = new Function(
        'index',
        'store',
        `
        return ${objectLiteral};
        `
    );

    return get;
}

function createAoSSetFunction(_schema: Schema) {
    return (index: number, store: any, value: any) => {
        store[index] = value;
    };
}

function createAoSFastSetChangeFunction(_schema: Schema) {
    return (index: number, store: any, value: any) => {
        let changed = false;
        if (value !== store[index]) {
            store[index] = value;
            changed = true;
        }
        return changed;
    };
}

function createAoSGetFunction(_schema: Schema) {
    return (index: number, store: any) => store[index];
}

const noop = () => {};
const createTagNoop = () => noop;

export const createSetFunction = {
    soa: createSoASetFunction,
    aos: createAoSSetFunction,
    tag: createTagNoop,
};

export const createFastSetFunction = {
    soa: createSoAFastSetFunction,
    aos: createAoSSetFunction,
    tag: createTagNoop,
};

export const createFastSetChangeFunction = {
    soa: createSoAFastSetChangeFunction,
    aos: createAoSFastSetChangeFunction,
    tag: createTagNoop,
};

export const createGetFunction = {
    soa: createSoAGetFunction,
    aos: createAoSGetFunction,
    tag: createTagNoop,
};

events (runQuery), event state is not cleared, so another query created later with same factory would see the same events and include them. Is that
correct? Current trait-level behavior: dirtyMasks/changedMasks persist, so a second query with same factory created after first query run would also
see past events. E.g., `Added` factory created, entity adds Foo, query1 runs and drains; query2 `Added(Foo)` created after would still match because
initial populate uses dirtyMask/current? Actually for Added, query2 created after entity already has Foo and oldMask 0, current bit set -> matches,
even though query1 drained. So yes, persistent. Pair state also persists. Good.

Potential issue: `hasPairEvent` for `Removed` doesn't check snapshot/current. For a query created after factory and after removal, event state has
removal -> matches. Good. For query created after removal but factory created after removal (no event), event state empty -> no match. Good.

describe('pair tracking modifiers across reset', () => {
    const world = createWorld();

    it('pair factories keep working after reset', () => {

        child2.add(Likes(parent2));

        const entities = world.query(Added(Likes(parent2)));

});
